### Empty-list gate does not cover the back-office country switch, where the stale previous country's list is non-empty

**Warning Severity**

`isTypeListLoaded` infers "loaded" from non-empty maps, but the back-office hook (`house-billing.hook.ts` `useRegistrationTypesByCategory`) uses `keepPreviousData: true`, so during a country switch the schema receives the previous country's non-empty list and the not-offered check runs against the wrong list — exactly the state the PR description claims the gate protects against. A registration type valid for the new country entered (or a row whose type is edited) during the in-flight window is flagged "This type is not offered in the billing country" and Save is blocked until the fetch resolves and revalidation reruns. The hook already computes the correct signal (`areRegistrationTypesLoaded`, which accounts for `isPreviousData`) but never feeds it to the schema, unlike the app-host hook which passes `[]` while loading/erroring.

**Fix:**
```
Have `useRegistrationTypesByCategory` return `EMPTY_REGISTRATION_TYPES` (or have the back-office hook pass `[]`) while `!areRegistrationTypesLoaded`, so the schema's empty-list gate also covers the previous-data window, mirroring the app-host behavior.
```

comments.author: robinthiry-naboo
comments.body:
### [ARCH-001] The load signal is inferred from data content, while both callers already hold the real one — Medium

**Confidence:** HIGH

The invariant this comment asserts is false in two reachable cases:

**1. A country that offers no registration types at all.** The gate then stays off permanently. `listRegistrationTypes` returns `[]` for a country outside the taxonomy, the server rejects *every* type (`validTypesByCategory[BUSINESS] ?? new Set()`), and the schema still requires at least one business registration. Net result: an unsaveable form, the generic toast, and no row named — precisely the symptom RAR-1403 targets, left unfixed on that country.

**2. The back-office country switch.** `useRegistrationTypesQuery` runs with `keepPreviousData: true`, and `house-billing.hook.ts:189-196` feeds the schema the **ungated** lists — even though the hook already computes `areRegistrationTypesLoaded` (which accounts for `isPreviousData`) and applies it only to the select options at `:315-320`.

On case 2 specifically, and to correct the bot's earlier assessment on this thread: the practical impact is much smaller than stated there. During the in-flight window Save is *already* blocked by `onFormValid(!areRegistrationTypesUnavailable)` and the select renders no options, so nothing new can be entered and the wrong error is transient and self-clearing. Case 1 is the permanent one, and the one worth fixing.

Worth noting `app-host` already handles this correctly: `registrationTypesForBillingCountry === null` yields `[]` to the schema *and* refuses the submit at the hook boundary. Only the back-office diverges.

**Fix.** Reusing the signal that already exists closes case 2:

```ts
// packages/womie-backoffice/.../house-billing.hook.ts:189
const schema = useMemo(() => {
  return getHouseBillingSchema({
    intl,
    businessRegistrationTypes: areRegistrationTypesLoaded ? businessRegistrationTypes : [],
    taxRegistrationTypes: areRegistrationTypesLoaded ? taxRegistrationTypes : [],
  })
}, [intl, areRegistrationTypesLoaded, businessRegistrationTypes, taxRegistrationTypes])
```

Case 1 needs the boolean passed explicitly rather than derived — an `isTypeListLoaded` param on `getHouseBillingSchema`, fed by `areRegistrationTypesLoaded` in the back office and by `registrationTypesForBillingCountry !== null` in app-host. The comment then disappears along with the inference.

The inference and its comment are gone; a country loaded with no type at all is covered by a new test.

**Confidence:** MEDIUM

comments.author: robinthiry-naboo
comments.body:
### [BUG-001] Countries with no taxonomy get every row flagged, with the wrong cause — Medium

**Confidence:** HIGH

**Issue:** The gate tests "the query resolved", not "it returned something". `REGISTRATION_TYPES_TAXONOMY` (`packages/wome-api/src/domain-modules/listing/house/sub-modules/house-billing/domain/constants/registration-type-taxonomy.constants.ts`) covers 119 of the 245 `Iso3166Alpha2Enum` members, even after `21cdddec1b0`. For the other 126, `listRegistrationTypes` returns `[]`, the query succeeds, the gate flips to `true`, and every row gets "This type is not valid for this section".

That is deliberate — `be6e975e709` says so — but the copy misstates the cause: the section has no valid type because **the country has no taxonomy at all**, which is not a section problem. The API words the same condition better: `HBL_INVALID_REGISTRATION_TYPE` → "not available for your billing address country".

**Impact:** Not a saveability regression — `businessRegistrations` is `min(1)`, the select has no options, and `validateRegistrationTypes` already refused server-side, so the form was a dead end before this PR; it now fails inline instead of through a toast. But the admin reads a cause that is false and has no way to clear it.

**Fix:** Either restore a per-section `validationMap.size > 0` guard (the test `flags a tax type when the country offers business types only` depends on the current behaviour and would need reworking), or keep the behaviour and split the copy: a "this country offers no registration type" message when both lists are empty, the section message otherwise.

### [TEST-002] The "previous country list" fixture is the incoming country's list — Low

**Confidence:** HIGH

**Issue:** The test is named *while the previous country list is still served*, but it serves `GERMAN_HRB_TYPE` (`countryIsoCode: DE`) while the house, the billing address and the row are all French — `buildBilling` defaults to an `FR` address with a `SIREN` business registration. In the scenario the name describes (user switches FR → DE, `keepPreviousData` keeps serving the FR list) the served list would *contain* `SIREN`, and the test would pass with or without the guard. Inverting the fixture is exactly what makes the branch observable, so the test is effective — the name just describes a situation the setup does not reproduce.

**Fix:** Either rename to what it actually asserts — `holds the not-valid check while react-query still serves a stale type list` — or make the switch explicit: render with `houseCountryIsoCode: Iso3166Alpha2Enum.DE` and `buildBilling({ address: { ...countryIsoCode: DE } })` while the row keeps the outgoing `SIREN`. `GERMAN_HRB_TYPE` then reads as the incoming list and `isPreviousData` as the in-flight window.

reviews.author: robinthiry-naboo
reviews.body:
## PR Review — APPROVE

No blocking issues. 5 advisory findings; two of them (ARCH-001, UX-002) are worth a call before merge, because they leave the ticket's symptom intact on one reachable path.

**What holds up well:** the refinement mirrors the server rule faithfully — `validateRegistrationTypes` also validates **per category** against `listRegistrationTypes({ countryIsoCode })`, so the client is never stricter than the server. The `path: [index, 'type']` shape composes correctly with react-hook-form (same shape as the shipped `refineUniqueTypes`), and there is no collision with the clearing effect in `registration-entries-field.tsx`: that effect only fires on a country *change*, while this check targets stored data at load — the two cases are disjoint.

**On zod semantics**, settled empirically against the installed **zod 4.5.4** (not v3 — in v4 checks live on the schema and are skipped only on an `aborted` payload, which a non-abort `.min(1)` does not produce): `superRefine` on `z.array(objectSchema)` *does* still run when an element failed its own `.min(1)`. So the reorder makes a row with a not-offered type and an empty value emit two issues — but on two distinct paths (`.value` and `.type`), one message per field, nothing overwritten. That behaviour is correct. See TEST-003 for the one thing missing around it.

### Top findings

- **[ARCH-001] Medium** — `isTypeListLoaded` infers load state from data content, while both callers already hold the real signal. A country offering **zero** registration types leaves the gate off permanently, so the generic-toast bug this PR fixes survives there. Inline on `house-billing.types.ts:217`.
- **[UX-002] Medium** — the billing form never maps `HBL_INVALID_REGISTRATION_TYPE`, so every path where the client gate is off still shows the generic toast. A message for that exact label already exists in the repo. Detailed below (the file is outside this diff).
- **[TEST-003] Low** — the only structural change in the diff (moving the not-offered check above the `!entry.value` guard) has zero coverage; verified by reverting the order and watching all four new tests still pass.
- **[TEST-004] Low** — two tests `.map()` away the message `getIssues` returns, so a regression emitting a *different* message on the right field keeps them green.
- **[UX-005] Low** — a type the country *does* offer, but in the other category, reads as "not offered in the billing country".

---

### [UX-002] The generic toast survives on every path where the client gate is off — Medium

**Location:** `packages/womie-backoffice/src/components/templates/list/houses/house/forms/house-billing-form/house-billing.hook.ts:47-72` (outside this diff, hence not inline)
**Confidence:** HIGH

`getBillingErrorMessage` maps `HBL_INVALID_REGISTRATION_VALUE`, `HBL_ADDRESS_RESOLUTION_FAILED` and `HBL_UNRESOLVED_BILLING_COUNTRY`, but not `HBL_INVALID_REGISTRATION_TYPE` — the label `InvalidRegistrationTypeError` actually raises (`house-billing.error.ts:29`). It therefore falls through to `bo.houseBilling.updateError`, "Error updating the billing information" — the exact toast RAR-1403 set out to replace.

A dedicated message for that label already exists at `house-billing-import-messages.ts:79` ("This registration type is not configured for the billing country"), wired for the CSV import modal but never for the form.

**Impact:** whenever the client-side check does not apply — the ARCH-001 zero-type country, or a failed `registrationTypes` query — the admin is back to the opaque toast with no row named.

**Fix:** one more branch in `getBillingErrorMessage`, on the model of the three already there. Client-only, ~5 lines. Strictly outside the ticket's scope ("No server change" still holds — this is not a server change), but it is the safety net under the fix.

---

### Conventions / ADR

No MUST/SHALL violation. Boolean naming, the dedicated `*Params` type, destructuring in the signature, early returns, ADR 004 / 024 / 037: all compliant. ADR 008 does not match these paths. The replaced test (`skips pattern validation for types not in the provided list`) covered the behaviour this PR retires — not lost coverage, and both states of the new boolean are re-covered.

---

reviews.author: robinthiry-naboo
reviews.body:
## PR Review — APPROVE

No blocking findings. Five advisory ones; the first two are worth settling before merge, because they concern what a reviewer believes they are approving.

- **The PR description promises a guard the code no longer has** — removed on purpose two commits later (detailed below, no file to anchor it to)
- **Countries with no taxonomy get every row flagged**, with a message that names the wrong cause
- `typeNotOfferedMessage` no longer describes the condition the branch tests
- **No hook-level test** covers the `keepPreviousData` / `loading` window — the exact regression the code comments warn about
- app-host re-inlines a derivation already named 40 lines below in the same file

---

### [DOC-001] The description announces a guard removed in `be6e975e709` — Medium

**Confidence:** HIGH

**Issue:** The PR body states *"The check only runs once either of the country's type lists is non-empty (a country can offer business types and no tax type)"*. That held at `7299f428f11`, which set `isTypeListLoaded = businessValidationMap.size + taxValidationMap.size > 0`. `be6e975e709` dropped it for the `areRegistrationTypesLoaded` flag passed by the callers, and says so itself: *"The schema inferred 'loaded' from non-empty type lists, which left the not-offered gate off for a country with no registration type"*. The test `flags every type once the country is loaded with no type at all` pins the opposite of what the description claims.

**Impact:** A reviewer signs off on a guard that is not there, and misses the empty-taxonomy case raised in the inline comment on `house-billing.types.ts`.

**Fix:** Rewrite that paragraph around the real flag (`areRegistrationTypesLoaded`, derived from `!isPreviousData` in the back office and from `loading || error` in app-host) and state the empty-list behaviour explicitly.

---

### Verified, nothing to report

- **Both gates are correct** in every window I could construct. Back office (`query-core@4.41.0`): `queryObserver.js:304` requires `status !== 'error'` before carrying previous data over, so an error leaves `data` undefined and the gate false; a country switch yields `isPreviousData: true` and the gate false. app-host (`@apollo/client@3.14.0`): `useResubscribeIfNecessary` resets `resultData.current = void 0` during render as soon as the variables change, so there is no render with `loading === false` over the previous country's list.
- **Rendering:** `getTypeOptions` prepends the current value as an option when it is missing from the list, so the offending row shows `FR-SIREN` rather than a placeholder; `SelectField` renders `ErrorMessage` under the select, so the `businessRegistrations.<i>.type` path lands in the right place; the remove button stays rendered.
- The early `continue` suppresses nothing: `refineUniqueTypes` is a separate loop and the `min(1)` checks live on the object schema. The `useMemo` deps are correct and referentially stable. RHF does not revalidate on a resolver identity change, so the gate flipping `false → true` cannot retroactively invalidate a form.
- **i18n: nothing to do.** `packages/i18n/lang/` is gitignored, the `@formatjs/cli-lib` AST extraction recognises the `intl.formatMessage({ id, defaultMessage })` shape, and keys are pushed to SimpleLocalize on merge to `dev`. Checked against the sibling id `duplicateRegistrationType` (`e90573bb1e7`): no catalogue file in that commit. English `defaultMessage`, so ADR-024 §1 holds.
- Perf: the loop is bounded by `REGISTRATIONS_MAX_SIZE = 10`.
- **Deduplicated** (already posted by `naboo-ai-reviews[bot]` and fixed since): ARCH-001, UX-005, TEST-003, TEST-004.

---

reviews.body:
## PR Review — APPROVE (second pass)

All five findings from the [first pass](https://github.com/naboo-team/naboo/pull/17609#pullrequestreview-5315219383) are resolved. One residual finding, Low, on test readability — inline below. CI is green, 64/64.

| Finding | Status | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| **DOC-001** description | Resolved | Now describes the real gate (`!isPreviousData` in the back office, `!loading && !error` in the partner app) and the new country-level message. |
| **BUG-001** countries with no taxonomy | Resolved | `hasRegistrationTypes = business.size + tax.size > 0` (`house-billing.types.ts:222`) picks between `typeNotValidForSectionMessage` and `noRegistrationTypeForCountryMessage`. Gating on the *union* is the right call: a business-only country with a stray tax row still reads "not valid for this section", which is true — the country does offer types. |
| **CONV-001** naming | Resolved | `rejectedTypeMessage` as the param, both messages as explicit consts, all six occurrences. |
| **CONV-002** duplicated derivation | Resolved | `areRegistrationTypesUnavailable` hoisted to `:162` and reused by the `useMemo`, which also takes it as a dep. |
| **TEST-001** load window | Resolved | Both halves, mutant killed — see below. |

### TEST-001 — mutation analysis

For `areRegistrationTypesLoaded = Boolean(data) && !isPreviousData`: the `Boolean(data)` half was already pinned (`house-billing.hook.test.tsx:388`, `:401`); the `!isPreviousData` half is pinned by the new test at `:621`. Delete `!isPreviousData` and the flag turns `true`, `businessValidationMap` holds only `HRB`, the `SIREN` row misses, the issue fires and `toBeUndefined()` fails. The `rerender()` path is sound: `useZodForm` rebuilds the resolver every render and react-hook-form 7.66 reassigns `control._options` unconditionally, so `trigger()` evaluates the new schema. On the app-host side all three cases are there — `loading`, `error`, and a positive control — and they assert the **per-row** error rather than `isSaveDisabled`, so the two "held" tests cannot pass vacuously.

### Verified, nothing to report

- **i18n:** `noRegistrationTypeForCountry` uses the same static inline shape as its siblings — both messages are formatted, then a ternary picks one — so extraction sees two literals. No catalogue edit needed; `Translation keys diff` and `Pull i18n translations` pass.
- **Mock hygiene:** `resetMocks` gained `isPreviousData` in this push and already covered the two app-host fields; `beforeEach` is wired on every top-level describe including the new one.
- **Style:** neither test file imports `screen` globally, `getUnknownTypeError` mirrors the existing `dirtyCompanyName` helper, and the `as const satisfies` fixture typechecks.
- **`44 passed`** is exact: 30 plain `it()` plus 14 cases from the four `it.each` (3+3+4+4). The earlier `42` was the stale number.
- No react-query v4/v5 mismatch: `isPreviousData` is the v4 API and the package is on `^4.42.0`.

RAR-1403 Billing form: name the row whose registration type is not offered by the billing country

Found while reviewing [RAR-1229](https://linear.app/naboo-team/issue/RAR-1229/the-dedicated-save-endpoint-and-the-narrow-write-behind-it) (PR [naboo-team/naboo#17490](https://linear.app/naboo-team/review/featapi-add-the-confirmation-time-business-registration-save-rar-1229-8e0dbbcabbe1), thread BUG-102). ## Problem A stored registration whose type is not offered by the stored billing country (e.g. `FR-SIREN` under a `DE` address) makes the billing form unsaveable with the generic toast "Error updating the billing information". The row is visible and editable, but nothing tells the admin which row is wrong. The state is reachable today through the CreditSafe autofill (address written, no filable registration) followed by a partner-filed registration under another country ([RAR-1229](https://linear.app/naboo-team/issue/RAR-1229/the-dedicated-save-endpoint-and-the-narrow-write-behind-it) / [RAR-1230](https://linear.app/naboo-team/issue/RAR-1230/the-registration-modal-shown-before-booking-confirmation)), and more generally whenever a stored type stops being offered by its country. The clearing effect in `registration-entries-field.tsx` only runs on a country *change*, never on load, and the client zod schema does not check that a type belongs to the country's list. ## Fix A zod refinement in `refineTypePatterns` (`packages/feature-views/src/features/house-billing/house-billing.types.ts`): when the country's type list is loaded and a row's type is not in it, add an issue on that row's `type` ("This type is not offered in the billing country"). Save then shows the error under the offending select and never reaches the server. Covers the back-office form and the partner billing page, which share `getHouseBillingSchema`. No server change: the save endpoint keeps reading nothing from the stored billing, and `validateRegistrationTypes` keeps refusing an invalid document.
